touches.text: A device talks to other devices only over the bus, never by importing them.

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).
There is no builder device. The builder is a CC session (or aider, 13), and the chart stages it uses are machines inside CodeMother.

VERBS: activate, charter, cross, deposit, drain, feedback, question, sealed (plus get and show). Moving a ticket across its workflow is the ticket's own act; CodeMother's gates only answer it (3.3.4). [Q#81: The chart stages (orient through validate) and the verdict are machines inside CodeMother (9.3.2, 9.3.4), and none of these verbs writes one, so the builder reaches them by importing her code: the /chart skill's own instructions do, and so do CC's chart and verdict helpers (cairn/devices/cc/scripts/), which the cc proof reds under RULE 1. Should CodeMother answer a `chart` verb (one stage, or all seven from a spec) and a `verdict` verb here, so a builder asks over the bus instead?]

Owns the Claude Code hooks: mail check, the turn-shape and ask scans, the gates on record writes and deletes. Anything that adapts CC specifically to Cairn goes in the CC device, and every one of CC's scripts lives here.

Skills (skills/: cairnhelp, challenge, chart, commit, intent, sorted, ...) are Claude Code's. The deterministic parts move out of markdown into CC device verbs: a skill's OS-side work runs as a script, and CC's shim processes the result and injects it into the session. WHY: every habit captured that way is one CC no longer spends inference on, so CC gets faster; a first charting pass done in deterministic Python with no LLM until after saved about 90% of tokens, measured in real use.
